title: An idea, connected

scenes.title: Hub arrives
scenes.purpose: Present the single product, a graphite hub, rising out of a dark studio space while the camera moves down into a frontal product view
visuals: Three.js bevelled graphite hub with rim lighting on a stationary slate vignette
Three satellite pucks scale in on the orbit
HUB eyebrow in the mint accent
assets: scene.js (procedural Three.js geometry, no external textures)

beats.development: Hub rises from the void and turns its side port toward the camera. The camera eases down from a high angle and the HUB eyebrow fades in.
Hub settles level. The orbit ring appears and the three satellite pucks scale in one after another. The status light turns mint.

scenes.title: Threads connect
scenes.purpose: Show the idea becoming a system: lit threads draw from the hub to each node, and each node lights when its thread arrives
visuals: Tube threads drawn with a progressive draw range
A glowing signal head travels at each drawing tip
Node LED rings switch to the accent

beats.development: Left, rear and right threads draw out in a staggered order. Each node lights as its thread lands, and the camera settles into the frontal hold.

scenes.title: Lockup and hold
scenes.purpose: Land the readable copy and hold the connected system
visuals: Headline and sub-copy rise into the lower band, which the product never covers
Leader line draws from the status light, then its label appears

beats.development: Headline finishes settling and the sub-copy lands. The leader line draws to its end before the STATUS LIGHT · LINKED label fades in.
captions: ONE HUB · THREE THREADS · NOTHING EXTRA

beats.development: Still frame with all copy legible and every node lit
captions: ONE HUB · THREE THREADS · NOTHING EXTRA

findings: Motion is concentrated on the product. The camera move ends at 1.4s and all threads have drawn by 1.99s.
Copy enters only after the system is connected and is fully settled by 2.55s, before the 2.7s requirement.
justifiedHolds: 2.55–3.0s: a still product hold so the headline and labels can be read

notes: No reviewed preview recipe was supplied (tech.preview_recipes is absent), so this preview demonstrates the base style plus the source-frame background refresh.
Per the user's instruction, Blender was not used. The 3D product is rendered in the browser with Three.js.
